title: Cross-Tenant Event Tampering and Access Token Rotation via Missing Client Authorization
description: Authenticated administrative endpoints that mutate event properties (PATCH /api/admin/settings), rotate access tokens (POST /api/admin/events/token), modify token duration windows (PATCH /api/admin/events/token), and reset device sessions (POST /api/admin/settings/reset-sessions) accept arbitrary event identifiers and execute updates using the privileged Supabase service role client without verifying that the event belongs to the authenticated client tenant (client_id = session.clientId). An authenticated client user can modify settings, rotate tokens, alter guest shot quotas, or lock out guests belonging to any other client tenant.
root_cause: The handlers invoke getAdminUser() to ensure an active administrative session exists, but omit tenant ownership validation (verifying event.client_id === session.clientId when session.role === 'client') before executing service-role database updates.
intended_behavior: When an authenticated caller with role 'client' submits an event modification or token rotation request, the server must verify that the target event has client_id matching session.clientId, returning 403 Forbidden if the event belongs to another tenant or client.

trace.description: Authenticated HTTP PATCH endpoint accepts arbitrary event ID and configuration updates from caller
Fetches target event using supabaseAdmin service role without checking client_id against caller session
Executes update on events table by event id without tenant ownership authorization

evidence.description: Authenticates user session via getAdminUser() but fails to verify event.client_id matches session.clientId
Updates token duration and expiration on arbitrary eventId without client ownership check
Rotates access_token on arbitrary eventId without client ownership check
Updates theme sessionResetAt timestamp on arbitrary eventId without client ownership check

conditions.description: Caller possesses a valid authenticated session cookie (dazzwed_auth_session) with role 'client'
Multiple tenant clients exist with distinct client_id assignments in public.events

execution.attacker_perspective: A malicious or compromised client tenant user authenticated with role 'client' targeting another wedding organizer's event
instructions: Authenticate as client tenant A and capture session cookie dazzwed_auth_session
Send HTTP POST to /api/admin/events/token with JSON body {"eventId": "<client-b-event-uuid>"}
Send HTTP PATCH to /api/admin/settings with JSON body {"id": "<client-b-event-uuid>", "status": "archived"}
execution.observed_result: Database update succeeds with HTTP 200 OK. Client B's event access token is rotated and event status is updated to archived, locking out Client B's wedding guests without authorization.

remediation.strategy: Before executing updates in /api/admin/settings, /api/admin/events/token, and /api/admin/settings/reset-sessions, inspect getAuthSession(). If session.role === 'client', query or filter by client_id = session.clientId, returning HTTP 403 Forbidden with code 'FORBIDDEN' if the event does not belong to the authenticated client.

likelihood.reason: Requires an authenticated client session and knowledge or enumeration of another tenant's event UUID.

impact.reason: Permits unauthorized cross-tenant modification of event configuration, denial-of-service via token rotation and archiving, and unauthorized session resets across wedding events.

confidence.reason: Source code review across all four route handlers directly demonstrates unconstrained supabaseAdmin updates on caller-supplied event IDs without client_id scoping.

title: Unauthenticated Event Access Token Disclosure via Public QR Generation Route
description: The administrative QR code generation endpoint (GET /api/admin/qr) omits authentication controls. When invoked with an event slug without a token query parameter, the handler queries public.events for the event's secret access_token using the privileged service role client and renders an SVG or PNG QR code embedding the full guest URL including ?t=<access_token>. Any unauthenticated remote actor who knows or guesses a wedding event slug can extract the secret access token, bypassing the physical venue QR poster boundary.
root_cause: src/app/api/admin/qr/route.ts fails to call getAdminUser() or requireAdmin() to enforce an administrative session, and automatically queries and embeds the confidential access_token when omitted by the caller.
intended_behavior: GET /api/admin/qr must either strictly require an authenticated admin session (matching other /api/admin routes) or reject requests where a valid access_token is not explicitly supplied by an authorized caller.

trace.description: Unauthenticated HTTP GET request handler accepts slug query parameter without checking session
Queries public.events for access_token using supabaseAdmin service role when token is not provided
Returns rendered SVG image containing guest URL with secret access_token parameter to unauthenticated caller

evidence.description: GET handler lacks getAdminUser() or authentication middleware check
Retrieves confidential access_token directly from database on behalf of unauthenticated caller
Constructs guest URL embedding secret access token: ${origin}/e/${slug}${tokenQuery}

conditions.description: No authentication required (anonymous unauthenticated network caller)
Target event has access_token configured in public.events

execution.attacker_perspective: An unauthenticated remote attacker attempting to access a private wedding camera roll knowing only the public couple slug
instructions: Send an HTTP GET request to /api/admin/qr?slug=our-wedding&format=svg without session cookies or authorization headers
Inspect the returned SVG markup or decode the embedded QR image matrix URL
execution.observed_result: HTTP 200 OK returned with Content-Type: image/svg+xml. The SVG metadata and embedded QR matrix encode the full URL containing the private event access token (e.g., https://dazzwed.vercel.app/e/our-wedding?t=ABC12345).

remediation.strategy: Enforce session authentication in GET /api/admin/qr using getAdminUser(). If the user is unauthenticated or has role 'client' without ownership of the event matching the requested slug, return HTTP 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden.

code_changes.fixed_code:
const admin = await getAdminUser();
if (!admin) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 });

likelihood.reason: Wedding event slugs are often predictable (e.g. couple names) or shared on public wedding invitations.

impact.reason: Discloses the private event access token, completely bypassing guest link protection and allowing uninvited remote actors to register guest rolls and upload unauthorized media.

confidence.reason: Direct inspection of src/app/api/admin/qr/route.ts confirms the absence of authentication middleware and unconditional query and disclosure of access_token.
